newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie yet to find floor in 4-month slide.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie yet to find floor in 4-month slide.

text.p: *AUD starts week softer after losing almost 1/2 cent in European trading Friday before steadying courtesy of NY holiday
*Repeated failure at $0.7550 last week suggests four-month downtrend not over yet and analysts tip test of $0.7440 again
*No end in sight to RBA easing speculation either
*ANZ job ads today to give pointer to labour figs Thursday

"The target for the week should be a revisit of recent US$0.7430 lows, enroute to the broader target of 73 cents," he said, adding a US$0.7470/7505 range today should be seen as a prelude to further falls.
By 8.00 am (2200 GMT) the local dollar was looking vulnerable at US$0.7476/81 having retreated from US$0.7519/24 late here Friday.

On the crosses it held steady at 85.30/40 yen from 85.15/25 thanks to a firmer US$/yen, but fell away to C$1.0272/83 from C$1.0324/35 amid heavy two-way flows as investors adjusted to the Bank of Canada's recent move to a policy tightening stance.
The surprise Canadian hike focused minds on the A$'s eroding yields with most of the market here still expecting another cut in official rates in the next month or so.
The exact timing was tricky but most analysts favoured a move after inflation and wages data on July 23/24, provided both were as benign as expected.

A few die-hard dollar bulls clung to the hope the year-long easing cycle had ended, listing improving forward indicators of the economy and the currency's weakness itself among the reasons for the Reserve Bank to hold off. One of those forward-looking figures, ANZ job advertisements for June, is out today.
The series has been extremely volatile recently as a record 16.7 percent jump in ads in April was followed by a 7.3 percent fall in May, making it hard to detect the actual trend.

It has also made analysts reluctant to forecast the figure, but it was clear another fall would not bode well for a big bounceback in the June jobs report. This is released Thursday and analysts are looking for a relatively modest rise of 40,250 in employment following a shock 40,300 fall in May.
Anything less than forecast would be considered weak and should employment fall again the money market would move to price in an immediate rate cut. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
